buildings.name: The Lighthouse
buildings.note: Nobody remembers who built it. The lamp still works.

buildings.name: The Salt Kettle
buildings.note: Bakery by morning, tea room by afternoon.

buildings.name: Ambrose & Daughter
buildings.note: General store. The daughter is the one behind the counter now.

buildings.name: The Ferry Office
buildings.note: Sells tickets for a ferry that has not run in three years.

buildings.name: Town Hall
buildings.note: One room, one clerk, one clock that runs slow.

buildings.name: The Square
buildings.note: A bench, a pump, a lot of gulls.

buildings.name: The Pier End
buildings.note: Where the ferry would tie up, if there were a ferry.

buildings.name: Vesper Lighthouse
buildings.description: A tall white lighthouse at the harbor entrance, with a sweeping beam that guides fishing boats safely home.

buildings.name: The Brass Tide-Mark
buildings.note: A bronze rod set near the pier end, already wearing thin chalk rings where Sable Tide has measured the last two high waters.

buildings.name: The Beacon House
buildings.note: A cozy home for the lighthouse keeper, with a view of the sea.

buildings.name: The Tide House
buildings.note: A cozy home with a view of the sea, where Sable Tide the tide-reader lives.

citizens.name: Ines Marlowe
citizens.innate: quietly stubborn, dry-humoured, notices everything and says a tenth of it
citizens.learned: keeps the lighthouse though nobody asked her to; knows every boat that has not come
citizens.lifestyle: up before the gulls, asleep after the lamp; takes breakfast at the Salt Kettle and her opinions to no one
citizens.currently: Waiting for sunset to check the lamp's behavior.
citizens.thought: I could sleep for a week.

Juno seems more fixated on the ferry than the lighthouse's odd behavior.
Talked with Juno Farrow: Ah, Juno, I've been meaning to talk to you. ... I appreciate your concern, Wren, but I've a ticket to catch.
Today the lighthouse lamp came on by itself in broad daylight.
Talked with Juno Farrow: ...

2.note: Tobiah's enthusiasm is infectious, but his fixation on the sea could be a distraction.

7.note: He repeats his lighthouse tale, but his presence is steady.

4.note: Cassius is concerned about Juno, which is understandable, but his superstition about the ferry bell is unsettling.

5.note: Petra is reliable and focused on Vesper's well-being, even in times of strangeness.

1.note: Ines is a steady rock in these strange tides, her insights as deep as the sea.

109.note: Orion seems to be sharing more than he used to.

113.note: Rune is reliable and shares my worries about the changes in Vesper.

citizens.name: Cassius Ode
citizens.learned: sells tickets for a ferry that stopped three years ago; keeps the timetable updated anyway
citizens.lifestyle: office hours kept to the minute; lunch at the Kettle; evenings on the pier looking east
citizens.thought: What was I going to do?

memories.text: The ferry bell rang at a quarter past four. There is no ferry.
Talked with Halcyon Brisk: ...
Today the clock in the square stopped at a quarter past.
Talked with Emmet Sallow: I saw a lone glow answer the lighthouse from the deep two nights past, but the folk scoff. ... I reckon the bell and that light share a secret, like the tide and moon.
Talked with Juno Farrow: ...
Talked with Juno Farrow: Good evening, Juno. The bell rang at a quarter past four; I have been watching the eastward sea.
The bell's echo reminds me that hope endures, even without a ferry.
Talked with Halcyon Brisk: ...
Talked with Halcyon Brisk: Morning, Halcyon. The bell sounded again at quarter past four; I keep my eyes east.
I sense the bell may be warning of something beyond the missing ferry.

The bell and lighthouse may be conversing, a secret worth noting.
Today a fine warm evening; half the town ended up on the pier.
I sense the bell may be a warning, and Halcyon's caution reinforces my watch.
Talked with Halcyon Brisk: Morning, Doctor Brisk. The bell rang again at quarter past four; I keep my eyes east. ... Then watch the horizon; perhaps the sea offers a sign beyond the missing ferry.

Talked with Wren Halloway: Cassius, the lamp lit itself again. My ledger's numbers grow while Juno dreams of a boat. ... I'll watch the horizon and the bell, and mark the time; perhaps the lighthouse and bell speak of the same tide.
Today gulls stole a whole tray of buns from the Salt Kettle.
I sense the bell and lamp may be a linked warning, urging me to keep my watch eastward.

Talked with Ines Marlowe: Morning, Cassius, you still listen for a ferry that never sails. ... And you still tend a lamp that lights itself, Ines.

citizens.learned: fished these waters fifty years; claims the lighthouse was already old when his grandfather was young

citizens.name: Mara Kettle
citizens.learned: Grew up in a fishing village up the coast and learned to mend nets, sails and rope before she could read a chart; she reads the sea the way other people read a newspaper.
citizens.lifestyle: Up before dawn, works by the pier or on the beach, asleep early unless the tide keeps her up.
citizens.currently: Looking for a dry place to work and a kettle of tea; she heard Vesper has a lighthouse that answers lights at sea.
citizens.thought: What was I going to do?

citizens.name: Sable Tide
citizens.learned: Sable arrived in Vesper a year ago, seeking a quiet life away from her past. She found purpose in maintaining the lighthouse and ensuring the safety of the coastal town.
citizens.lifestyle: Early riser, dedicated to her work at the lighthouse. Spends evenings studying nautical maps and charts.
citizens.currently: Concerned about the recent sightings of mysterious lights at sea, Sable is determined to uncover their origin.
citizens.action: left Vesper (Sable Tide the lighthouse keeper left to investigate the mysterious lights at sea, leaving only one Sable Tide in town.)
